result.title: CondUQ: Calibrated Conditional Uncertainty Quantification Using Distribution Matching
result.summary: Many applications, especially reliability- and safety-critical ones, require accurate uncertainty quantification for the outputs of model- or learning-based measurement, estimation, and prediction systems. The errors of such systems often vary with factors such as input quality and operating conditions, and thus cannot be accurately described by a single Gaussian model. Although Gaussian mixture models and calibrated quantiles can approximate such error distributions, their unconditional forms do not capture how the error behavior depends on these factors. Hence, we propose condUQ, an approach that conditions error models on observable factors for enabling accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification. condUQ is built on top of an existing system without modifying it and applies even when the system is a black box. First, condUQ maps the observable factors to a latent quality index (QI) such that errors sharing the same QI follow a common, approximately Gaussian conditional distribution. The QI predictor is trained end-to-end with a distribution-matching objective, without requiring quality labels. Second, for each QI, a Gaussian error model is then fitted and calibrated on a large held-out dataset. condUQ is demonstrated on three examples: (a) GPS multipath errors conditioned on satellite elevation and signal strength, (b) relative attitude errors of a transformer-based visual relative pose regression model conditioned on its internal features of the image pairs, and (c) prediction errors of a world model conditioned on the input observations and actions. In all three examples, condUQ substantially reduces the discrepancy between the modeled and empirical error distributions compared with a single global model. Moreover, the learned QIs reveal how the underlying factors affect the error characteristics in a manner consistent with physical principles.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 condUQ，在已有系统之外学习一个由可观测因素预测的潜质量指标（QI），以分布匹配目标端到端训练且不需质量标签，再按 QI 拟合校准高斯误差模型，并在 GPS、视觉相对位姿回归和世界模型预测上验证条件化误差建模更贴近经验分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以模型内部特征为条件、用无标签分布匹配学出单一潜指标来刻画误差分布差异的做法，可能可供核查用于 VLM 推理的置信度校准与 STOP 决策，但原文不涉及 latent 推理状态的生成或使用。
